open_issues: Drag-and-drop of a .wakeel-setup file onto the window (MainWindow.HandleDrop -> SetupFileDrop -> W02) is still unexercised at runtime: a WPF drop cannot be synthesised over CDP. The path is covered only by the unit level (SetupFileDrop) and by reading the same file through the picker.

The disk-full state (Ar.FirstRun.Setup.DiskFull) is now produced from the real ERROR_DISK_FULL / ERROR_HANDLE_DISK_FULL HRESULTs in W02's staging, W02's inspection and W04's activation, but it is not covered by an automated test: filling a disk is not something the suite can stage. RecoveryService.RecoverAsync still folds a full disk into its general failure message.

ARCHITECTURE.md §3's MachineWrap remains DPAPI at LocalMachine scope with a constant entropy string, so any local account on the computer can unwrap DbKey from installation.key; the policy that it 'does not open the data on its own' is enforced in LockService rather than by cryptography. Implemented as specified; it is the specification that would need revisiting.
notes:
Every high, medium and low finding is fixed, plus the missing spec items that were in scope.

FINDING 1 (high) — ActivationService.ActivateAsync now returns an ActivationResult and refuses at the very top, before WriteKeyFile: `if (AlreadyActivated) return new ActivationResult(ActivationOutcome.AlreadyActivated, Ar.FirstRun.Account.AlreadyActivated)`, where AlreadyActivated is `File.Exists(InstallationKeyPath) || File.Exists(DbPath)`. W04 renders that sentence instead of throwing. W02SetupFile, W03SetupCheck and W04Account each gained the mirror of W05's guard in OnInitialized: `if (Login.IsActivated) Nav.NavigateTo("/login", replace: true)`. Proven two ways: a walkthrough test activates, offers a second checked file, and asserts the key file is byte-for-byte identical afterwards and that the old password and the old recovery code both still work; and live over CDP, navigating an activated machine to /first-run lands back on /login with no drop zone.

FINDING 2 (medium) — SetupInspectionService takes AccountSession and exposes ExpectationsAsync(): with no installation it returns SetupExpectations.FirstRun(StagingDirectory); with one it returns PinnedOrgSigningPub from Installation.OrgEd25519Pub, InstalledDeviceId and InstalledExportSeq from the settings. The device id is compared ordinally inside Wakeel.Crypto, so activation now also records the file's own spelling of it in a new setting (AccountSettingKeys.SetupDeviceId = "setup.device_id"); the installation row's Guid is the fallback. W02.InspectAsync calls ExpectationsAsync and passes the result. A walkthrough test activates, then asserts the product-supplied expectations carry all three, that a newer file for this device still passes, and that a genuinely different device's file (new identity, new certificate issued by the same organisation) is refused — so «هذه الحزمة أُعدّت لجهاز آخر» and «أقدم من المثبَّتة» are now reachable from product code.

FINDING 3 (medium) — W05 injects AccountOptions and runs PreCheckClock() in OnInitialized: ClockVerdict.Bad when now < BuildDate, or when the sealed card's LastSignInAt is set and now < LastSignInAt - ClockCheckService.BackwardTolerance. ClockCheckService still runs after sign-in so the check is recorded in clock_checks. Two bUnit tests pin both verdicts and the chip variant.

FINDING 4 (medium) — LoginService.SignInAsync, LockService.UnlockAsync and RecoveryService.Verify/RecoverAsync now catch every CryptoException around the key-wrap opens and branch on the code: WrongPassword keeps the counted wrong-password result, everything else (Corrupt, UnknownKind) becomes SignInOutcome.DatabaseUnreadable / RecoveryOutcome.KeysMissing with its Arabic sentence. A walkthrough test damages the key file's stored derivation settings and asserts sign-in returns a plain-Arabic message and Recovery.Verify — which W07 calls from a keystroke handler — does not throw.

FINDING 5 (medium) — W07's verification is now `await Task.Run(() => Recovery.Verify(code))` behind a _verifying flag, with «جارٍ التحقق من الرمز...» as the hint while it runs and the result dropped if the text changed meanwhile; ScanAsync goes through the same path.

FINDING 6 (low) — W04.StartAsync clears the two typed secrets on both paths but only clears Sheet on success; on failure it restores `Sheet = Activation.Sheet` so a retry still shows the code that a retry would activate with.

FINDING 7 (low) — the identity block and the «لست أنت؟» button are inside `@if (_profile.HasIdentity)`, and the footer uses the new Ar.FirstRun.Login.FooterLineWithoutDevice when DeviceNo is 0. Verified live: a folder with keys+db but no readable card renders product branding, no identity row, and «إصدار الوكيل v0.21» with no device number.

FINDING 8 (low) — LockService takes LoginService and now honours a standing lock-out at the top of UnlockAsync, routes its WrongPassword branch through LoginService.RecordWrongPassword, resets the counters on success, and writes the accumulated unlogged failures to the audit log once the database is open. A walkthrough test exhausts the attempts on the overlay, sees the lock-out refuse even the right password, waits it out, unlocks, and asserts the account.sign_in_failed entry.

FINDING 9 (low) — the two key buffers are declared before the try in all three services and zeroed in the catch as well as the finally.

FINDING 10 (low) — WakeelTestContext registers AddWakeelCore with WakeelPaths.ForRoot on a per-test temporary folder and deletes it on dispose.

FINDING 11 (low) — the isolate moved into the constant (Ar.FirstRun.Login.CapsLockHint now carries U+2066 «Caps Lock» U+2069, the same treatment SetupExtensionInline gets) and W05 renders it through <Bdi>. A bUnit test types an all-caps password and asserts the isolate survives into the DOM.

FINDING 12 (low) — new DiskSpace.IsFull(Exception) walks the inner chain for ERROR_DISK_FULL (0x70) / ERROR_HANDLE_DISK_FULL (0x27). W02 maps it to Ar.FirstRun.Setup.DiskFull in both staging paths and in the inspection; ActivateAsync returns ActivationOutcome.DiskFull with the same sentence, and W04 also catches it around the Task.Run.

MISSING SPEC ITEM (W07 sheet) — once the new sheet exists the dialog replaces the form with the sheet card (code, QR, issue date, owner) plus «طباعة الورقة الجديدة» and «حفظ الورقة الجديدة ملف PDF» wired to IPrintService; the confirming button becomes «حفظتُ الورقة الجديدة». W05 carries .w-no-print while the dialog is open, and W07's scoped stylesheet enlarges the square for the printed page, so what comes off the printer is the sheet and not the sign-in screen behind it.

BUILD AND TESTS — the prescribed command, run whole: Wakeel.Desktop 0 warnings / 0 errors; Walkthrough build 0/0; Walkthrough 15/15, Core.Tests 175/175, UI.Tests 209/209 (399 total). No NuGet package added; no file outside the allowed paths touched (the Admin, Crypto and Design-component changes in git status belong to other agents and were there at session start).

HOST RUN — both hosts launched, screenshotted, read and killed; no Wakeel.Desktop process left. Empty --data-folder on port 9351: /json/version answered, /json/list reported /first-run, W02 rendered (drop zone doubling as picker, package password with reveal, «فحص الحزمة», «أين أجد الملف؟»), the ProgramData layout came out complete, log holds one startup line. A folder carrying keys/installation.key and data/wakeel.db but no readable card on port 9352: /login, and the CDP screenshot and DOM read together give the live evidence for findings 7 and 3 — zero .w05-identity nodes, no «لست أنت؟», footer «إصدار الوكيل v0.21», branding «الوكيل», clock chip «ساعة الجهاز سليمة • الأربعاء 16/09/2026 — 16:23» which the pre-check actually reached rather than assumed. Screenshots were JPEG under 1366 px and looked at once each.
